bib.title: Enabling Conversational Interaction with Mobile UI using Large Language Models

question: Can a single prompted LLM enable several conversational interaction tasks on mobile UIs without task-specific datasets and training?
hypothesis: Few-shot prompting with an HTML text representation of the view hierarchy gives competitive performance across mobile UI tasks.
contributions: First investigation of LLMs for conversational interaction on mobile UIs.
A method to feed GUIs to text LLMs (view hierarchy to HTML via DFS) plus prompting techniques for a range of conversational tasks; code open-sourced.
Experiments on four tasks: Screen Question-Generation, Screen Summarization, Screen QA, Mapping Instruction to UI Action.

method.summary: Android view hierarchies are converted by depth-first traversal into HTML (class mapped to tags, resource_name into class attribute, content_desc into alt, numeric ids). A prompt is a task preamble, up to 2 exemplars (screen HTML, optional chain of thought, tagged output) and the test screen; PaLM is prompted with no training. Four tasks evaluated against a template, Screen2Words, DistilBERT and Seq2Act.
method.task: few-shot prompting of an LLM for mobile UI tasks (question generation, summarization, screen QA, instruction-to-action)

datasets.name: RICO (screen question-generation)
datasets.size: 400 test screens each with at least one EditText; 931 questions evaluated
datasets.preprocessing: leaf nodes visible to the user only in prompt

datasets.name: Screen2Words
datasets.size: more than 24k screens, five summaries each; test set 4310 screens from 1254 apps
datasets.split: Screen2Words test set; 2 random screens with one summary each as exemplars

datasets.name: Screen QA (preliminary, RICO screens)
datasets.size: 300 QA pairs from 121 unique screens; 288 after holding out 3 screens (12 QA pairs); 57 of 288 answers absent from view hierarchy
datasets.split: 1 pair sampled from each of the 3 held-out screens as exemplars
datasets.source: preliminary data from authors of ScreenQA [18]
datasets.preprocessing: focus on answers present in view hierarchy

datasets.name: PixelHelp
datasets.split: one screen per unique app package used as prompt modules; in-app vs cross-app

models.name: PaLM
models.architecture: LLM (decoder-only, per PaLM paper; not described here)
models.context: 1920 tokens max input; at most 2 exemplars

other.note: parameter count of the PaLM variant used not stated

inference.samples: one output per item; exemplar choice random, number of prompt draws or seeds not stated (PixelHelp prompts built from randomly sampled prompt modules)
inference.prompting: Preamble + N exemplars (N = 0, 1, 2) + test screen HTML; output wrapped in task tags (<SOQ>/<EOQ>, <SOS>/<EOS>, <SOA>/<EOA>, <SOI>/<EOI>); chain of thought only for Screen Question-Generation (input count given as ground truth, screen purpose, enumeration).

parameters.class_mapping: TextView to p; Button/ImageButton to button; ImageView to img; EditText to input; others to div
parameters.ids: numeric DFS index as id attribute

metrics.name: Grammar Correctness
metrics.definition: human rating of generated question, 5-point Likert

metrics.name: UI Relevance
metrics.definition: human binary judgement of question relevance to highlighted element

metrics.name: Question Coverage F1
metrics.definition: automatic: indices of ground-truth input elements vs those identified in chain of thought

metrics.name: Human preference (summarization)
metrics.definition: three annotators per screen choose more accurate summary: LLM, Screen2Words, or equal

metrics.name: Exact Matches / Contains GT / Sub-String of GT / Micro-F1
metrics.definition: string-match categories (mutually exclusive) and word-overlap micro F1 across dataset

metrics.name: Partial / Complete match
metrics.definition: percentage of partial and complete matches of target element sequences (as Seq2Act)

eval.protocol: Question generation: 17 raters (professional Google data labelers), three raters per question, 5% audit, Mann-Whitney U test. Summarization human study: 37 annotators, full test set, 3 ratings per screen. Others automatic. Single run reported.

availability.data: RICO, Screen2Words, PixelHelp are open; screen QA set is preliminary, from authors of [18]

prompts.text: Given a screen, the agent needs to identify the elements requiring user input and generates corresponding questions.
Given a screen, summarize its purpose.
Given a screen and a question, provide the answer based on the screen information.
Given a screen, an instruction, predict the id of the UI element to perform the instruction.

evidence.quote: The PaLM model is trained with a maximum input length of 1920 tokens.

results.claim: Screen summarization: LLM summaries judged more accurate than Screen2Words by majority vote on 64.1% of screens.
results.setup: 2-shot PaLM vs Screen2Words, Screen2Words test set, 3 annotators per screen
results.quote: LLM summaries are more accurate than those of the bench-
results.note: Fig 5 caption; text says 63.5% of individual annotations favoured LLM, 28.6% benchmark, 7.9% equal

results.claim: Unanimous preference for LLM summaries on 52.8% of screens vs 20.5% for the benchmark.
results.quote: Remarkably, LLM summaries were rated as more accurate unanimously by three annotators for 52.8 % of screens.

results.claim: Screen summarization automatic metrics: 2-shot LLM trails Screen2Words on all metrics (BLEU-1 45.0 vs 65.5).
results.table: Table 2, rows 2-shot LLM and Screen2Words, column BLEU-1

results.claim: Screen QA: 2-shot LLM reaches 66.7% exact match and 64.8% micro-F1 vs DistilBERT 36.0% and 37.2%.
results.setup: 231 = 288 - 57 inferred from answers present in view hierarchy; 2-shot PaLM; DistilBERT off-the-shelf
results.table: Table 3, row 2-shot LLM, column Exact Matches
results.note: Micro-F1 64.8 vs 37.2; 1-shot 65.8 EM, 62.9 F1; 0-shot 30.7 EM. n inferred; paper does not say how many of 288 were scored

results.claim: Zero-shot screen QA already works (30.7% exact match) while zero-shot summarization and instruction mapping fail.
Mapping instruction to UI action: best setting (2-shot, in-app) gets 80.36 partial and 45.0 complete vs Seq2Act 89.21 and 70.59.

Our best-performing

results.claim: Screen question-generation: LLM grammar 4.98 vs template 3.60 (p < 0.0001).
results.setup: 2-shot PaLM with chain of thought, 400 RICO screens, 931 questions, 3 raters each
results.quote:
Our approach achieves an almost perfect
average score of 4.98 on grammar correctness, while the rule-based
approach receives a 3.6 average rating.

results.claim: Screen question-generation: UI relevance 92.8% vs 84.1% template; coverage F1 95.9% (precision 95.4%, recall 96.3%).
results.setup: as above; template coverage 100% by construction

results.claim: The first exemplar gives most of the gain; the second adds little.
results.note: e.g. screen QA micro-F1 31.2 to 62.9 to 64.8

limits: Only view hierarchy used; fails where information is in pixels (icons without alt-text, photo-editing apps).
Single-turn unit conversations only; no multi-screen or multi-turn.
Prompt limited to at most 2 exemplars by PaLM 1920-token limit; HTML length varies widely.
Hallucination and steerability not addressed; no control over behaviors such as question combining.
Screen QA data is preliminary, 57 of 288 answers not in the view hierarchy; string matching under-reports aliased answers (9/15 vs September 15th).
Underperforms Seq2Act on instruction mapping; automatic summarization metrics favour the trained benchmark.
No decoding settings, PaLM size, seeds or variance reported; only one prompt draw per condition appears to be reported.
Chain of thought used only for question generation; authors say it did not help other tasks in early investigations, with no data shown.
